guide.title: How to get from Geneva to Gruyères: train, car and travel time
guide.description: Geneva to Gruyères: about 2 h 20 by train with one or two changes, about 1 h 30 by car via the A1, A9 and A12. Practical tips for your day out.
guide.h1: How to get from Geneva to Gruyères
guide.intro: Gruyères is about 120 kilometres from Geneva. By car, allow about an hour and a half without traffic. By train, allow about two hours twenty from Geneva station, with one or two changes. Here are both options in detail, and what to know once you arrive.

p: From Geneva station (Cornavin), you travel to Palézieux, often with a first change at Renens. From Palézieux, a regional train runs to Bulle and then to Gruyères. On the official timetable for a weekday in November 2026, morning journeys take between 2 h 22 and 2 h 34, with one or two changes. There is no direct train.
Gruyères station is in Pringy, at the foot of the hill. La Maison du Gruyère is very close to the station. The medieval town and the castle sit higher up: you walk up on a sloping path.
For Maison Cailler in Broc, you need another regional train from Bulle to Broc-Fabrique station. Timetables change every year in December: check the SBB timetable on sbb.ch for your date.

The route follows the A1 motorway along Lake Geneva to Lausanne, then the A9 towards Vevey and the A12 towards Bulle. After the Bulle exit, Gruyères is only a few kilometres away. Allow about an hour and a half, longer at rush hour around Geneva and Lausanne. The Swiss motorway vignette is compulsory.
In Gruyères, you explore the medieval town on foot. Leave the car in the car parks below, then walk up to the castle.

sections.h2: Train or car: which to choose?
p: The train saves you driving and looking for a parking space. However, visiting several places on the same day, such as Gruyères, Pringy, Broc and Moléson-sur-Gruyères, means planning your connections carefully.

A car gives more flexibility to move from one stop to the next, especially with children or in a group. For a private tour, we choose the format with you based on your group, before anything is confirmed.

The morning suits La Maison du Gruyère, as the cheese is made in the morning. Next come the medieval town and its castle. In the afternoon, the day continues at Maison Cailler, the HR Giger Museum or the Moléson, depending on the season and the weather.

tips: Check the train timetable on sbb.ch the day before: it changes every year in December.
Wear good shoes: the climb to the town is on foot, over cobblestones.
If you drive, remember the Swiss motorway vignette.
To see the cheesemaker at work, arrive at La Maison du Gruyère in the morning.
Check the Moléson opening dates before adding it to your plans.

faq.q: How long does the train take from Geneva to Gruyères?
faq.a: About two hours twenty to two and a half hours, with one or two changes, often at Renens and Palézieux. Times vary by day: check them on sbb.ch.

faq.q: Is there a direct train between Geneva and Gruyères?
faq.a: No. You need to change at least once, usually at Palézieux, where the regional train to Bulle and Gruyères departs.

faq.q: How long does it take by car?
faq.a: About an hour and a half for 120 kilometres, via the A1, A9 and A12. Allow more time at rush hour around Geneva and Lausanne.

faq.q: Can you see Gruyères and Maison Cailler on the same day by train?
faq.a: Yes, but you need one more regional train between Gruyères, Bulle and Broc. Plan your connections in advance, or send us a private tour request.
